exercises.q: She is looking forward to ____ you next week.
exercises.why: After 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so use -ing.

exercises.q: My manager wants me ____ the report today.
exercises.why: 'Want somebody' is followed by to + infinitive.

exercises.q: I'm not used to ____ up so early.
exercises.why: 'Be used to' + -ing means being accustomed to something.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: I look forward to meet you.
I look forward to meeting you.
I look forward to meet with you.
exercises.why: 'Look forward to' needs -ing: meeting.

exercises.q: He promised ____ late for work again.
exercises.why: 'Promise' + (not) to + infinitive.

exercises.q: Stop ____ (check) your phone every five minutes!
exercises.why: 'Stop' + -ing means ending an activity.

exercises.q: We managed ____ (fix) the server before the users noticed.
exercises.why: 'Manage' is followed by to + infinitive.

exercises.q: She is interested in ____ (learn) Python.
exercises.why: After a preposition, use the -ing form.

exercises.q: I remember ____ (lock) the door, so someone else must have opened it.
exercises.why: 'Remember' + -ing refers to a past memory.

exercises.q: Estou ansioso para ir para Londres.
exercises.ans: I am looking forward to going to London.
exercises.why: 'Look forward to' + -ing.

exercises.q: Ele recusou-se a assinar o contrato.
exercises.ans: He refused to sign the contract.
exercises.why: 'Refuse' + to + infinitive.

exercises.q: Você se importa de fechar a porta?
exercises.ans: Do you mind closing the door?
exercises.why: 'Mind' is followed by -ing.

exercises.q: She is waiting ____ the bus stop.
exercises.why: Use 'at' for a specific point or place.

exercises.q: I'm ____ a train to Rio right now.
exercises.why: We say 'on' a train, bus, plane or ship.

exercises.q: The office is ____ 25 Rose Street.
exercises.why: Use 'at' with a full address including the number.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: I will travel in July on 2025.
exercises.why: Use 'in' for months and years.

exercises.q: He is very good ____ solving problems.
exercises.why: The fixed expression is 'good at'.

exercises.q: The conference is ____ March.
exercises.why: Use 'in' with months.

exercises.q: I never work ____ Sundays.
exercises.why: Use 'on' with days of the week.

exercises.q: She is afraid ____ flying.
exercises.why: The fixed expression is 'afraid of'.

exercises.q: The meeting starts ____ noon.
exercises.why: Use 'at' with clock times and noon.

exercises.q: Nos vemos na segunda-feira de manhã.
exercises.why: Use 'on' with a day plus part of the day.

exercises.q: O livro está na prateleira.
exercises.ans: The book is on the shelf.
exercises.why: Use 'on' for a surface.

exercises.q: Eu cheguei em casa às oito da noite.
exercises.ans: I got home at eight in the evening.
exercises.why: 'At' for clock time, 'in' for parts of the day.

exercises.q: She ____ swim when she was five.
exercises.why: 'Could' expresses past ability.

exercises.q: You ____ smoke in the hospital. It is forbidden.
exercises.why: 'Mustn't' expresses prohibition.

exercises.q: ____ I borrow your pen, please?
exercises.why: 'Could I...?' is a polite request for permission.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
exercises.why: After a modal, use the base verb with no 'to' and no -s.

exercises.q: You ____ see a doctor. You look very sick.
exercises.why: 'Should' gives advice.

exercises.q: She ____ speak three languages. (ability, present)
exercises.why: 'Can' expresses present ability.

exercises.q: Passengers ____ leave bags unattended. (prohibition, one word)
exercises.why: 'Mustn't' means it is forbidden.

exercises.q: ____ you like some tea? (polite offer)
exercises.why: 'Would you like...?' is a polite offer.

exercises.q: I'm sorry, I ____ come to your party. I have to work. (negative of can)
exercises.why: Negative of 'can' is can't or cannot.

exercises.q: Posso entrar?
exercises.why: 'May I...?' asks for permission politely.

exercises.q: Você não precisa pagar agora.
exercises.ans: You don't have to pay now.
exercises.why: 'Don't have to' means no obligation.

exercises.q: Eu não consegui abrir o arquivo.
exercises.why: 'Couldn't' is the past of 'can't'.

exercises.q: If I ____ a million dollars, I would travel the world.
exercises.why: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + verb.

exercises.q: She would be happier if she ____ her job.
exercises.why: The if-clause uses past simple, not 'would'.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: If I would have time, I would help you.
If I had time, I would help you.
If I have time, I would help you.
If I will have time, I would help you.
exercises.why: Never use 'would' in the if-clause: if I had time.

exercises.q: If the servers ____ faster, users wouldn't complain.
exercises.why: Past simple (were) after 'if' for an unreal present.

exercises.q: What ____ if the internet stopped working for a week?
exercises.why: Result clause: would + subject + base verb in questions.

exercises.q: If I ____ (live) closer to work, I would walk every day.
exercises.why: Past simple in the if-clause.

exercises.q: He ____ (be) much calmer if he slept more.
exercises.why: Result clause uses would + base verb.

exercises.q: If it ____ (not/rain), we would go to the beach.
exercises.why: Negative past simple in the if-clause.

exercises.q: If I were rich, I ____ (buy) an island.
exercises.why: Result clause: would + base verb.

exercises.q: Se eu ganhasse na loteria, eu pararia de trabalhar.
exercises.ans: If I won the lottery, I would stop working.
exercises.why: If + past simple, would + verb.

exercises.q: O que você faria se perdesse o emprego?
exercises.ans: What would you do if you lost your job?
exercises.why: What would + subject + do + if + past simple.

exercises.q: Se ele falasse mais devagar, eu entenderia.
exercises.ans: If he spoke more slowly, I would understand.
exercises.why: If + past simple, would + base verb.

exercises.q: If I ____ harder, I would have passed the exam.
exercises.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect.

exercises.q: We would have won if we ____ the penalty.
exercises.why: Past perfect in the if-clause.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: If I would have known, I would have called.
If I had known, I would have called.
If I knew, I would have called.
If I have known, I would call.
exercises.why: Do not use 'would have' in the if-clause.

exercises.q: If the backup ____ properly, we wouldn't have lost the data.
exercises.why: Unreal past needs past perfect.

exercises.q: She wouldn't have missed the flight if she ____ earlier.
exercises.why: Past perfect in the if-clause.

exercises.q: If he ____ (not/forget) the password, he would have logged in.
exercises.why: Negative past perfect: hadn't forgotten.

exercises.q: They would have bought the house if it ____ (be) cheaper.
exercises.why: Past perfect of 'be' is 'had been'.

exercises.q: If you had called, I ____ (pick up).
exercises.why: Result: would have + past participle.

exercises.q: If we had taken a taxi, we ____ (arrive) on time.
exercises.why: Result: would have + past participle.

exercises.q: Se eu tivesse acordado cedo, não teria perdido o ônibus.
exercises.ans: If I had woken up early, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
exercises.why: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

exercises.q: Se tivéssemos testado o código, não teríamos tido esse erro.
exercises.ans: If we had tested the code, we wouldn't have had this error.
exercises.why: Past perfect, then wouldn't have + past participle.

exercises.q: Ela teria ido se tivesse recebido o visto.
exercises.ans: She would have gone if she had received the visa.
exercises.why: Would have + participle, if + past perfect.

exercises.q: If I hadn't skipped breakfast, I ____ hungry now.
exercises.why: Past condition, present result: would + base verb.

exercises.q: If she didn't speak English, she ____ the job at the US firm.
exercises.why: Present state, past result: would have + participle.

exercises.q: If I were a better driver, I ____ the accident last week.
exercises.why: Present trait (were) with a past result.

exercises.q: If we ____ the contract last year, we would be in a stronger position today.
exercises.why: Past perfect in the if-clause, would + verb for the present.

exercises.q: Which sentence is a mixed conditional?
opts: If I had gone, I would have seen him.
If I had gone to the party, I would be tired today.
If I went, I would see him.
If I go, I will see him.
exercises.why: Past if-clause with a present result.

exercises.q: If he ____ (be) more patient, he wouldn't have shouted at the client.
exercises.why: Present unreal trait uses 'were'.

exercises.q: If I hadn't moved to Berlin, I ____ (not/know) my wife now.
exercises.why: Present result: would + base verb.

exercises.q: If she ____ (take) the medicine, she would feel better now.
exercises.why: Past perfect for the past condition.

exercises.q: If the team were more experienced, they ____ (make) that mistake yesterday.
exercises.why: Past result: would have + past participle.

exercises.q: Se eu tivesse estudado medicina, seria médico agora.
exercises.ans: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
exercises.why: Past perfect, then would + base verb.

exercises.q: Se ele fosse mais cuidadoso, não teria apagado o banco de dados.
exercises.ans: If he were more careful, he wouldn't have deleted the database.
exercises.why: Present trait, past result.

exercises.q: Se não tivéssemos perdido o voo, estaríamos na praia agora.
exercises.ans: If we hadn't missed the flight, we would be on the beach now.
exercises.why: Past condition, present result.

exercises.q: The emails ____ every morning by the system.
exercises.why: Present simple passive: are + past participle.

exercises.q: The bridge ____ built in 1990.
exercises.why: Past simple passive: was + past participle.

exercises.q: The problem ____ right now.
exercises.why: Present continuous passive: is being + participle.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: The room was cleaned by the staff yesterday.
The room cleaned by the staff yesterday.
The room was clean by the staff yesterday.
exercises.why: The passive always needs 'be' plus the past participle.

exercises.q: The new policy ____ announced yet.
exercises.why: Present perfect passive: has been + participle.

exercises.q: The documents ____ (sign) by both parties last week.
exercises.why: Past simple passive, plural subject.

exercises.q: The server ____ (update) at the moment.
exercises.why: Present continuous passive.

exercises.q: The patch ____ before release. (must / test)
exercises.why: Modal passive: modal + be + participle.

exercises.q: This building ____ (design) by a famous architect in 1920.
exercises.why: Past simple passive.

exercises.q: O contrato foi assinado ontem.
exercises.why: Was + past participle.

exercises.q: Meu laptop está sendo consertado.
exercises.why: Is being + past participle.

exercises.q: Todos os funcionários serão avisados.
exercises.why: Future passive: will be + participle.

exercises.q: 'We were late,' they said. They said they ____ late.
exercises.why: Past simple backshifts to past perfect.

exercises.q: 'Don't touch it,' she told me. She told me ____ it.
exercises.why: Negative commands: told + object + not to + verb.

exercises.q: 'Where is the station?' he asked. He asked where ____.
exercises.why: Reported questions use statement word order.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: She said me that she was busy.
She told me that she was busy.
She told that she was busy me.
She said to that she was busy.
exercises.why: 'Tell' needs an object; 'say' does not take one directly.

exercises.q: 'I'll send it tomorrow,' he said yesterday. He said he ____ it the next day.
exercises.why: 'Will' backshifts to 'would'.

exercises.q: 'Do you like sushi?' she asked. She asked me ____ I liked sushi.
exercises.why: Yes/no questions are reported with if or whether.

exercises.q: 'I have lost my keys,' he said. He said he ____ lost his keys.
exercises.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect.

exercises.q: 'Close the window,' the teacher said. The teacher told us ____ close the window.
exercises.why: Reported commands use to + infinitive.

exercises.q: 'I'm working today,' she said. She said she ____ working that day.
exercises.why: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous.

exercises.q: Ele disse que ligaria mais tarde.
exercises.ans: He said he would call later.
exercises.why: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech.

exercises.q: Ela me perguntou onde eu trabalhava.
exercises.ans: She asked me where I worked.
exercises.why: Reported question: no do-support, backshifted tense.

exercises.q: O chefe nos pediu para chegar cedo.
exercises.ans: The boss asked us to arrive early.
exercises.why: Asked + object + to + infinitive.

exercises.q: She hasn't answered the email. She ____ it yet, or she would have replied.
exercises.why: 'Can't have' + participle: past deduction of impossibility.

exercises.q: The data is wrong. Someone ____ it by mistake.
exercises.why: 'Must have' + participle: strong past deduction.

exercises.q: We took a taxi, but it was unnecessary. We ____ have taken a taxi.
exercises.why: 'Needn't have' means it was not necessary but it happened.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
exercises.why: Modal + have + past participle, with no 'to'.

exercises.q: I deleted the wrong file. I ____ have been more careful.
exercises.why: 'Should have' expresses regret about the past.

exercises.q: That ____ be Paul. He is in Paris this week. (impossible)
exercises.why: 'Can't be' expresses a present deduction of impossibility.

exercises.q: I'm not sure where he is. He ____ have gone to lunch. (possible, one word)
exercises.why: Might/may/could have express past possibility.

exercises.q: You ____ have bought a gift. It wasn't necessary, but thank you! (one word)
exercises.why: 'Needn't have' or 'shouldn't have' are polite thanks.

exercises.q: The ground is wet. It ____ have rained last night. (almost certain)
exercises.why: 'Must have' is a strong past deduction.

exercises.q: Ele pode ter esquecido a senha.
exercises.ans: He might have forgotten the password.
exercises.why: Might have + past participle.

exercises.q: Eu devia ter ligado antes.
exercises.why: Should have + past participle shows regret.

exercises.q: Ela não pode ter feito isso.
exercises.why: Can't have + past participle.

exercises.q: I wish I ____ speak French.
exercises.why: Wish + could for an ability you lack.

exercises.q: I wish it ____ so cold today.
exercises.why: Wish + past form for a present situation.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: I wish I have more money.
I wish I had more money.
I wish I would have more money.
I wish I will have more money.
exercises.why: Wish about the present uses past simple.

exercises.q: If only we ____ the backup before the crash!
exercises.why: Past regret: past perfect.

exercises.q: I wish my boss ____ me work from home. He never agrees, and it annoys me.
exercises.why: Wish + would for annoying behavior you want to change.

exercises.q: I wish I ____ (be) taller.
exercises.why: Present wish: were (or was).

exercises.q: She wishes she ____ (not/accept) the offer last year.
exercises.why: Past regret: negative past perfect.

exercises.q: If only I ____ (have) a car right now!
exercises.why: If only + past simple for a present wish.

exercises.q: I wish you ____ (stop) interrupting me.
exercises.why: Wish + would for an annoying habit.

exercises.q: Eu gostaria de saber dirigir.
exercises.why: Wish + could for ability.

exercises.q: Se ao menos eu tivesse estudado mais!
exercises.ans: If only I had studied more!
exercises.why: If only + past perfect for a past regret.

exercises.q: Eu queria que ele parasse de fazer barulho.
exercises.ans: I wish he would stop making noise.
exercises.why: Wish + would + verb for annoyance.

exercises.q: The woman ____ car was stolen called the police.
exercises.why: 'Whose' shows possession.

exercises.q: The report, ____ I read yesterday, was excellent.
exercises.why: Non-defining clauses use 'which', never 'that'.

exercises.q: She passed all her exams, ____ surprised everyone.
exercises.why: 'Which' can refer to a whole clause.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: The man who I spoke to him is my boss.
The man who I spoke to is my boss.
The man which I spoke to is my boss.
The man what I spoke to is my boss.
exercises.why: Do not repeat the object after the relative pronoun.

exercises.q: The city in ____ I grew up is very small.
exercises.why: After a preposition use 'which', not 'that'.

exercises.q: The engineer, ____ team built the system, got a promotion.
exercises.why: 'Whose' links a person to what belongs to them.

exercises.q: He arrived late, ____ made the manager angry.
exercises.why: 'Which' refers to the whole previous clause.

exercises.q: The hotel ____ we stayed was near the beach.
exercises.why: 'Where' refers to a place.

exercises.q: The people with ____ I work are very friendly.
exercises.why: After a preposition, use 'whom' for people.

exercises.q: O livro cujo autor eu conheci está esgotado.
exercises.ans: The book whose author I met is sold out.
exercises.why: 'Whose' replaces 'cujo'.

exercises.q: Ela perdeu o voo, o que a deixou muito irritada.
exercises.ans: She missed her flight, which made her very angry.
exercises.why: ', which' refers to the whole clause.

exercises.q: A cidade onde nasci fica no sul.
exercises.ans: The city where I was born is in the south.
exercises.why: 'Where' refers to a place.

exercises.q: ____ the door, he noticed a strange smell.
exercises.why: Present participle for simultaneous or active actions.

exercises.q: The students ____ the exam were nervous.
exercises.why: Present participle replaces 'who were taking'.

exercises.q: The software ____ by our team is very reliable.
exercises.why: Past participle has a passive meaning.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence (common mistake):
opts: Having finished the report, she went home.
Having finish the report, she went home.
Finished the report having, she went home.
Had finishing the report, she went home.
exercises.why: Having + past participle shows an earlier action.

exercises.q: ____ money, he couldn't buy a ticket.
exercises.why: Having + noun gives a reason.

exercises.q: ____ (read) the instructions, he started the machine.
exercises.why: Having + past participle: the reading came first.

exercises.q: The man ____ (talk) to the manager is my uncle.
exercises.why: Present participle for an ongoing action.

exercises.q: ____ (not/know) the password, she called the IT team.
exercises.why: Negative: Not + -ing.

exercises.q: The photos ____ (take) at the wedding are beautiful.
exercises.why: Past participle with passive meaning.

exercises.q: Sentindo-se doente, ele ficou em casa.
exercises.ans: Feeling sick, he stayed at home.
exercises.why: Present participle clause giving a reason.

exercises.q: A carta escrita por ela chegou ontem.
exercises.ans: The letter written by her arrived yesterday.
exercises.why: Past participle replaces 'which was written'.

exercises.q: Tendo perdido o ônibus, ela pegou um táxi.
exercises.ans: Having missed the bus, she took a taxi.
exercises.why: Having + past participle for a prior action.

exercises.q: Rarely ____ such dedication.
exercises.why: After negative adverbs, invert auxiliary and subject.

exercises.q: Only after the update ____ the bug.
exercises.why: 'Only after' at the start triggers inversion with do-support.

exercises.q: Little ____ that the system would crash.
exercises.why: 'Little' at the start requires inversion.

exercises.q: Should you need help, ____.
exercises.why: 'Should you...' replaces 'If you should...'; the main clause is an imperative.

exercises.q: Not until he got home ____ his wallet.
exercises.why: 'Not until' at the start triggers inversion in the main clause.

exercises.q: Seldom ____ (we/see) such good results.
exercises.why: 'Seldom' + auxiliary + subject.

exercises.q: Not only ____ she smart, but she is also kind.
exercises.why: 'Not only' + inverted verb be.

exercises.q: At no time ____ the company inform customers of the breach. (past)
exercises.why: 'At no time' + did + subject + base verb.

exercises.q: ____ you have any questions, please contact us.
exercises.why: Inverted conditional: Should you = If you should.

exercises.q: Nunca vi tanta gente neste escritório.
exercises.ans: Never have I seen so many people in this office.
exercises.why: 'Never' + have + subject + participle.

exercises.q: Só depois da reunião percebi o erro.
exercises.ans: Only after the meeting did I notice the mistake.
exercises.why: 'Only after' + did + subject + base verb.

exercises.q: Em nenhum momento ele pediu desculpas.
exercises.ans: At no point did he say sorry.
exercises.why: 'At no point' + did + subject + base verb.
